title.narrative: Number of Agreements signed between EU and stakeholders

description.narrative: (Institutional dialogue): Agreements signed between EU and SEA stakeholders state of ratification ofcomprehensive aviation agreements between the EU and South East Asia (ASEAN) states, MOUs

comment.narrative: Number of agreements signed 201216
Increase of 1 agreement signed 201722

An amendment of the MoU was signed between EASA and Indonesia DGCA on airworthiness matters in March 2019 to expand the scope as a result of several project activities organised for the benefit of DGCA Indonesia. A MoC between EASA and CAAS on aviation health safety measures in relation to the COVID19 pandemic was signed on 22 July 2020 to frame the cooperation on the compilation and exchange of COVID related data. This MoC should be considered outside of the scope of the project however due to the global relevance of the procedure and material developed and implemented by EASA together with ECDC it has been adopted by many third countries. The working arrangement with CAAS on airworthiness certification was amended on 24 November 2020 to allow CAAS to join EASA as an observer in certification activities which will allow a faster validation of EU products in Singapore effectively lowering the barriers for market access in Singapore of EU products. Although only indirectly linked to the project the negotiations for the ASEANEU Comprehensive Air Transport Agreement AE CATA were concluded and the agreement signed in October 2022. An MoU between CAAS and EASA on collaboration on urban air mobility was signed in October 2022 to support the development deployment and safe operation of vertical takeoff and landing VTOL aircraft. An MoU between ATMRI Singapore and EASA on artificial intelligence particularly in the fields of UAMUAM And UTM was signed in March 2023.

comment.narrative: Number of EU bilateral regional interregionaland multilateral cooperation partnershipstrategies as of 2017
Number of EU bilateral regional interregionaland multilateral cooperation partnershipstrategies which have been enhanced by 2022

Partnership strategies enhanced during 2018 and 2019 bilateral cooperation with Thailand and Indonesia Regionalcooperation with COSCAP SEA and ASEAN and International and regional cooperation with ICAO Asia and Pacific Office inBangkok have continued during 2020 establishing periodic videoconference contact with them to minimise the lack ofonsite activities.1Bilateral with the Civil Aviation Authority of Thailand started in 2018. The project has an office with personnel workingin their premises what allows a constant exchange and a very close relation with the EU institutions EASA and EU DelBangkok2Regional with COSCAPSEA started in 2018. The project is in constant communication with the coordinator of theprogramme and a relation of trust has been stablished. In addition since mid of 2019 a training programme coorganisedbetween the EU SEA APP and COSCAPSEA is being implemented containing both regional and bilateral activities.3 Regional with ASEAN Secretariat started in 2018. Together with the other projects that EASA is implementing in theregion Specially ARISE a very fluent communication has been established with the ASEAN secretariat who have beeninvited as key actor in the region to participate and contribute to the main events organised by the project in the regionICAOEASA Forums Project Management Boards. In 2020 it is planned to organise the Project Management Board of theSEA APP back to back to the ATTCATWG meeting which is the main regional technical meeting on aviation that theASEAN Secretariat organises every year.4Interregional with the ICAO Asia and Pacific Office in Bangkok started in 2018 what can be proved by the coorganisedICAOEASA Forum on Civil Aviation in South East Asia yearly high level event.5 Bilateral with DGCA Indonesia.
